saint_reference.note: Simon is best known in the New Testament as the name of Saint Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles.

data.cultural_impact: Simon was an everyday name in the Middle East over 2,000 years ago, and it's still used today, albeit less frequently than it once was. The name has cultural significance in Christian tradition as the original name of Saint Peter, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus. Simon was a fisherman by trade, and according to the New Testament, Simon was given the name Peter by Jesus after they met. The name Simone or Simona is more commonly used for females, and Simon is predominantly given to males.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Simon is steeped in spiritual significance in Christianity, as it represents one who hears or listens. This holds great importance as Jesus often spoke of the need to listen and respond to His teachings. In the New Testament, Saint Peter was given the name Rock, which represented his steadfastness as a disciple and leader within the Christian community. This name change also symbolizes the transformation and strengthening that occurs when we listen to and act upon the Word of God.
